title: Apply the canonical same-origin path check to saved draft resume routes
detail: The local safeRoute check refused // but accepted slash-backslash and slash/control/slash forms that URL normalization resolves to another origin. Drafts uses the stored route in router.push. Reuse the pure lib/auth/safe-next.ts validator instead of maintaining a weaker copy, while retaining the existing trim, 300-character limit and null fallback. The same seam validates writes, individual loads and the draft list, so legacy unsafe stored routes are suppressed without a data migration. Three behavioral regressions prove the sample paths resolve off-site under URL parsing and must be rejected at every store boundary; all three failed on the previous code. This is owner-scoped resume-path hardening: no cross-user injection or live exploitation was demonstrated. Final focused validation: 126 tests in eight suites passed, including canonical path validation, draft sync/recovery and the bin action. No production data or schema changes. Probe-cost correction on 2026-10-23: the prior ledger command reran the full test runner (node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --cache=false --fsModuleCachePath .next/cache/audit-vitest --maxWorkers=2 lib/studio/draft-store.test.ts lib/auth/safe-next.test.ts). Keep those comprehensive behavior tests in normal CI; the ledger now executes the actual code/fixture consequence directly without a nested runner. No assertion or application gate is waived.

verify.note: Three URL-normalization cases must be null on staged writes, individual resume reads and list reads. Existing valid paths, owner scoping, draft save failures and canonical auth destination rules remain covered. Normal CI retains the fuller test suites; this direct probe keeps the per-row guard bounded.
